papers.title: Age- and sex-related variation in TREC and KREC and the association of rs2204985 with TREC in adults
papers.abstract: Background: T-cell receptor excision circles (TREC) and kappa-deleting recombination excision circles (KREC) are indirect markers of new T- and B-cell production. Recorded zero values complicate the analysis of age-related and genetic associations in adult cohorts. Methods: We analyzed 574 adult outpatients aged 39-95 years, including 250 men and 324 women. TREC and KREC were quantified by multiplex real-time PCR and normalized per 100,000 cells. The rs2204985 variant was evaluated using age- and sex-adjusted genetic models. A two-part model separated TREC positivity from quantitative TREC levels among participants with positive values. Alternative regressions and receiver operating characteristic analyses were used for sensitivity and age-classification analyses. Results: Age was more strongly associated with log10(TREC + 0.1) than with log10(KREC + 0.1) (beta = -0.0365 and -0.00728 per year, respectively). Women had higher levels in the main-effects models, although the KREC age association differed by sex. There was no clear evidence of an additive rs2204985 association with TREC positivity (odds ratio = 0.836, p = 0.290). Among the 481 TREC-positive participants, the G allele was associated with higher log10(TREC) (beta = +0.0688 per allele, 95% CI +0.0177 to +0.1199, p = 0.0084; q = 0.0126 across three conditional genetic-model tests). Smearing-corrected marginal predictions for a 58-year-old woman were 40.4 copies/100,000 cells for AA and 53.5 for GG. In the common-positive subset (n = 465), TREC showed higher age-classification AUCs than KREC or their ratio. Conclusions: The rs2204985 association was apparent in conditional TREC levels but not in recorded positivity or full-cohort regression. Analyzing these outcomes separately makes the association easier to interpret, without establishing that zero TREC denotes absent thymopoiesis or that the variant directly alters thymic function.

papers.title: Local macrophage and cDC1 cooperation in the liver drives T-cell immune surveillance against pioneering metastatic cancer cells.
papers.abstract: The liver is one of the most frequent sites for hematogenous metastasis across different types of cancer, but how the liver mounts effective immune responses against arriving tumor cells is not fully understood. Using intravital imaging, we have visualized the initial steps of liver metastasis and delineated three phases in the immune response at the earliest stages of liver metastasis: first, there is continuous surveillance of the liver parenchyma by discrete immune cell subsets in the premetastatic tissue. Second, upon metastatic cell arrival, there is massive neutrophil recruitment and tumor-cell material uptake mediated by resident macrophages. Third, antitumor-specific T-cell activation takes place in situ within intrahepatic leukocyte clusters. We find that tumor-derived material uptake triggers transcriptional programs in liver myeloid cells that upregulate chemoattraction programs in Kupffer cells and cDCs, leading to T-cell activation. Antigen cross-presentation and a functional partnership between cDC1s and local macrophages to recruit and form T-cell activation clusters are required for the elicitation of these intrahepatic T-cell responses. Consequently, prior expansion of cDCs by Flt3L-Ig treatment significantly enhances immunosurveillance, curtailing successful metastasis development. Collectively, our findings identify coordinated immune responses that are essential for anti-metastatic immunity within the liver, uncovering a program to mount defenses against tumor cells arriving in the liver.

papers.title: VisioWell, an all-in-one high-throughput platform to study haematopoietic cells division
papers.abstract: Live-cell imaging has the potential to unravel crucial parameters for haematopoietic normal and leukaemic stem and progenitor cells. Yet, this technology requires a combination of technical and analytical skill sets that can be difficult to find in a traditional haematology lab. We present VisioWell, an all-in-one experimental platform specifically designed to measure the early division dynamics of blood stem and progenitor cells, from a simple brightfield long-term acquisition. We combined a simple custom-made microwell array to trap thousands of individual cells with a powerful semi-automatic analytical pipeline, able to segment, correct, and retrieve the division times for the first three sets of divisions. We validated VisioWell with primary cells from human cord blood and with a cellular model of myeloid leukaemia, revealing that CDK4/6 inhibition induces an increase in asynchronous division. By lowering the technical and analytical barriers to live-cell imaging, VisioWell makes label-free, non-destructive analysis of division dynamics accessible to any haematology lab, while preserving cells for downstream fate and functional readouts.

papers.title: Modular innate recognition in conventional T cells through FcRγ reconstitution
papers.abstract: Engineered T cells can elicit durable tumor responses but largely rely on TCRs or CARs for target recognition. Here we show that FcR{gamma}, an innate signaling adaptor not expressed by conventional T cells, enables full-length innate receptor function in adult human {beta} T cells. FcR{gamma} reconstitution enabled endogenous NKp30 surface expression and cytotoxicity without inducing an innate-like state. Stable co-expression of NKp30 and FcR{gamma} maintained receptor expression after activation withdrawal, supported sustained tumor killing, delayed leukemia progression in mice, and enabled cytotoxicity against primary myeloid leukemia. FcR{gamma} also supported functional import of receptors spanning natural cytotoxicity, Fc receptor, and C-type lectin families, extending conventional T cell responses to tumor ligands, antibody-coated targets, IgE receptor engagement, and microbial patterns. These findings establish a shared-adaptor strategy for expanding innate recognition in engineered T cells while preserving the identity and functional properties of the widely adopted conventional T cell platform.

papers.title: Dynamic T-cell receptor repertoire remodeling is associated with murine and human lung allograft dysfunction
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is a major cause of late graft failure after lung transplantation. Acute cellular rejection is an established risk factor for CLAD. However, its diagnosis by biopsy may incompletely capture dynamic and spatially heterogeneous immune remodeling within the allograft. We investigated whether lung graft proximal T-cell receptor beta-chain (TCR{beta}) repertoire features reflect alloimmune remodeling and associate with acute cellular rejection (ACR) and CLAD. TCR{beta}; sequencing was performed on graft-infiltrating T-cells from a murine orthotopic lung transplant model and on 90 longitudinal bronchoalveolar lavage cell-pellet (BAL-cp) samples from 23 lung transplant recipients during the first post-transplant year. In the murine model, allografts showed persistent histologic injury and strong, consistent TCR{beta}; repertoire remodeling relative to isografts. Across days 28 and 56, murine allografts had higher productive clonality (Cliff's {delta}; = 0.93, p = 0.0087) and maximum productive frequency (Cliff's {delta}; = 0.93, p = 0.014), with complete rank separation at each time point. Murine allografts also exhibited greater pairwise Morisita repertoire overlap (p < 0.0001) and enrichment of recurrent, high-frequency shared clonotypes. Productive clonality from human lung transplant recipients' BAL-cp was higher at the a priori selected month-6 visit from patients who developed CLAD, as compared to those who remained CLAD-free (p = 0.0326). In a month-6 surveillance-visit index analysis, high productive clonality was associated with early onset CLAD (CLAD within 2 years of transplant) (log-rank p = 0.038). In a patient-specific index-event analysis, CLAD-free survival differed across high and low productive clonality groups among acute rejectors (log-rank p = 0.019). Together, these findings establish measurable graft-localized TCR{beta}; repertoire remodeling and position BAL TCR{beta}; profiling as a potential complement to biopsy diagnosis. With validation in larger cohorts, graft-proximal repertoire measures may help identify CLAD-associated immune states before the onset of lung function decline and inform more individualized surveillance.

papers.title: Terminally differentiated CX3CR1+ natural killer cells drive coronary arteritis through an NFAT-T-bet axis
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells acquire potent effector function through terminal differentiation, yet the signals driving this program toward pathogenicity in vascular inflammation remain undefined. Using an FK565-induced mouse model of Kawasaki disease and single-cell transcriptomics from patients, we identify NK cells as major drivers of coronary arteritis through cytotoxicity and CCL5-CCR1-mediated recruitment of myeloid cells. This activity is concentrated in a terminally differentiated, T-bet-driven NK cell subset, the cardiac accumulation of which depends on CX3CR1, and a corresponding population is enriched in patient transcriptomic datasets. We further identify signaling through calcineurin and nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT) as an upstream driver of this program, with NFATc1 induced in NK cells. Calcineurin inhibition suppressed T-bet induction, reduced this subset and attenuated disease development. These findings define an NFAT-T-bet-CX3CR1 axis that couples terminal NK cell differentiation to coronary inflammation.

papers.title: Xist deletion in T cells protects against influenza-induced lung injury
papers.abstract: Sex differences in antiviral immunity are well established, yet the contribution of X-Chromosome Inactivation (XCI) to T cell responses during infection is unknown. Here, we identify an unexpected role for Xist RNA in shaping T cell immunity and pulmonary injury following influenza infection. We show that the inactive X chromosome (Xi) in pulmonary CD4+ and CD8+ T cells undergoes dynamic epigenetic remodeling, with limited Xist RNA localization, differential enrichment of H3K27me3 and H2AK119Ub modifications, and activation-dependent XCI escape of immune-related genes, including Il2rg and Cxcr3. Remarkably, T cell-specific Xist deletion protects female mice from influenza-induced weight loss and pulmonary pathology despite comparable early viral burdens. Transcriptomic profiling reveals increased expression of X-linked escape genes and antiviral and interferon-responsive genes, particularly in CD8+ T cells. Furthermore, Xist-deficient CD4+ and CD8+ antigen-experienced (CD44+CD11a+) T cells exhibit increased biallelic Cxcr3 expression, elevated pulmonary Cxcr3 protein levels, and enhanced IFN-{gamma} and TNF responses following ex vivo stimulation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for Xist RNA in regulating female antiviral T cell responses and demonstrate that enhanced T cell effector potential can accompany reduced infection-associated pulmonary injury.

papers.title: Deciphering the role of adenosine-related genes in regulating smooth muscle cell phenotypic switch in coronary heart disease via single-cell RNA sequencing
papers.abstract: Background: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is closely associated with dysregulated lipid metabolism, inflammation, and impaired adenosine signaling. However, the contribution of adenosine-related genes (ARGs) and their relationship with the immune microenvironment remain unclear. Methods: Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with curated ARGs. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified candidate genes, and XGBoost, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination, and Boruta were used to select diagnostic features. Gene set enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory-network, and single-cell RNA-sequencing analyses were performed, followed by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction validation. Results: We identified 4,884 differentially expressed genes and 243 ARG-associated module genes, yielding 231 candidate genes. DYRK2 and SIGIRR were prioritized as key genes and were consistently downregulated in bulk CHD datasets, including the validation cohort. A two-gene nomogram showed strong diagnostic performance. Functional analyses linked both genes to mitochondrial dysfunction and innate immune regulation, while immune profiling indicated reduced adaptive immune populations and enhanced myeloid-associated inflammation. Single-cell analysis identified smooth muscle cells as a key compartment with altered DYRK2 and SIGIRR expression along pseudotime trajectories and remodeling of vascular endothelial growth factor and pleiotrophin signaling. Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction in clinical samples (n = 5 per group) supported the bioinformatic expression trends (P < 0.05). Conclusions: DYRK2 and SIGIRR emerged as key adenosine-related genes associated with immune-metabolic imbalance and smooth muscle cell dysfunction in CHD. These findings provide a basis for further mechanistic and translational validation.

papers.title: Distinct innate immune states associate with divergent serological outcomes after syphilis treatment
papers.abstract: The global resurgence of syphilis poses a major public health challenge, even in the era of effective antibiotic therapy. Following treatment, some patients achieve seroreversion, whereas others remain serofast with persistent nontreponemal antibody reactivity. Although nontreponemal antibody titers guide clinical follow-up, it remains unclear how closely they reflect the resolution of inflammation and recovery of immune function. We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, immunophenotyping in clinical samples, and functional assays to characterize circulating monocytes and natural killer (NK) cells across seroreversion and low- and high-titer serofast states, and further examined the impact of HIV coinfection. CD14+ monocytes retained inflammatory and CD163-associated scavenging programs after seroreversion, whereas serofast patients showed additional IFN-STAT1 activation in this subset. NK cells from serofast patients exhibited reduced JUN expression and impaired degranulation. JNK inhibition reduced the magnitude and altered the kinetics of NK cell degranulation, IFN-{gamma} production, and amphiregulin (AREG) induction. Among low-titer serofast patients, HIV coinfection was associated with higher mitochondrial complex I gene expression and partially restored NK cell degranulation compared with patients with syphilis alone. Complex I inhibition also reduced NK cell degranulation. These findings suggest that seroreversion does not necessarily indicate immune normalization and identify post-treatment immune alterations not fully captured by conventional serological monitoring, providing a rationale for investigating cellular immune markers as complementary measures of recovery after syphilis treatment.

papers.title: A Beta-to-Alpha seasonal coronavirus antibody signature identifies high and low responders to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination
papers.abstract: Pre-existing immunity to endemic seasonal human coronaviruses may shape subsequent responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We longitudinally profiled 775 healthcare workers using a systems immunology machine learning framework and found that a recursive feature elimination cross-validation model classified individuals in the top and bottom quartiles of SARS-CoV-2 Spike IgG responses (AUC=0.72, empirical P<0.001). This predictive signature was prominently driven by a baseline bias toward Beta-coronavirus relative to Alpha-coronavirus Spike reactivity.

papers.title: A Novel Autoantibody against LAG-3 in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by immune tolerance loss, although its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Immune checkpoint molecules maintain peripheral tolerance, and their dysregulation contributes to autoimmunity. Autoantibodies against lymphocyte activation gene-3 (LAG-3), an immune checkpoint molecule, were identified in a subset of patients with SLE. We enrolled 130 patients with SLE, 119 patients with other autoimmune diseases, and 32 healthy controls. The sera of patients with SLE were screened for antibodies against various immune checkpoint molecules to identify clinically relevant disease-specific autoantibodies against LAG-3. Functional assays were performed to assess the effect of anti-LAG-3 autoantibodies on the interaction between LAG-3 and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II. Pathogenic relevance was evaluated using genetic deletion and immunization-based mouse models. Anti-LAG-3 autoantibodies were detected in 52/130 patients with SLE (40.0%) but only 4 of 119 patients with other autoimmune diseases (3.4%). These autoantibodies were associated with lupus nephritis and higher disease activity. In mice, Lag3 deletion or human LAG-3 immunization induced lupus-like autoimmunity. These findings support the clinical relevance of anti-LAG-3 autoantibodies in SLE and implicate LAG-3 checkpoint disruption in lupus-like autoimmunity.

papers.title: Resident liver macrophages buffer dietary and circulating cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis
papers.abstract: Cholesterol metabolism is viewed largely through the lens of hepatocytes, leaving the roles of other liver cells unclear. Using high-resolution live imaging and cholesterol tracing in intact zebrafish, complemented by genetic and clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion and single-cell analysis, we identify liver-resident macrophages (LMs) as cellular buffers of circulating and dietary cholesterol. LMs directly take up cholesterol, and their depletion redirects cholesterol to hepatocytes, which suppress cholesterol synthesis, increase bile-acid synthesis and efflux, and activate metabolic-stress and immune programs, including hepatokine lect2 induction. These responses are heightened by elevated dietary cholesterol and occur without overt inflammation or altered liver architecture. LMs partition cholesterol through abca1b-dependent export and cetp-mediated lipoprotein remodeling. Loss of abca1b causes cholesterol sequestration in LMs and reduced cholesterol-processing demand on hepatocytes, while LM depletion eliminates macrophage-derived cetp and reduces hepatocyte cetp. Together, these findings reveal the innate immune system as integral to normal metabolic physiology, with LMs buffering cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis.

papers.title: The MHC requirement for αβ T-cell specification is heterochronically gated
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-dependent thymic selection is a defining principle of {beta} T-cell development, yet mice lacking {beta}2m-dependent MHC class I and MHC class II retain rare {beta} T cells whose developmental significance has remained unresolved. Here we show that this residual compartment is not simply the product of failed selection. Single-cell and clonotypic profiling resolves distinct outcomes, including clonally restricted CD4-associated states and a diversified CD8 {beta} T-cell population that converges on physiological wild-type virtual memory. These CD8 cells lack conventional self-MHC calibration, retain broad T-cell receptor (TCR) diversity, respond rapidly to T-cell receptor and cytokine stimulation, and confer protection during bacterial infection. Their preservation is developmentally restricted: the MHC-independent state carries a neonatal transcriptional and phenotypic imprint, is favored by fetal but not adult progenitors, and is reduced by neonatal Lin28 inhibition. While these data do not displace the central requirement for MHC in generating the conventional naive {beta} T-cell repertoire, they establish that {beta} T-cell specification can proceed during early life in its absence, yielding a physiological and functionally competent CD8 {beta} T-cell fate. Thus, the MHC requirement for {beta} T-cell specification is heterochronically gated.

papers.title: Tumor cell-intrinsic AHR sustains IFNγ responsiveness and durable CD8 T-cell-mediated melanoma control
papers.abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) regulates melanoma differentiation and progression, but its tumor cell-intrinsic role in T-cell immunotherapy remains incompletely understood. Since AHR promotes inflammation-induced melanoma dedifferentiation, we hypothesized that AHR deficiency would reduce resistance to adoptive CD8 T-cell therapy (ACT) targeting melanocytic differentiation antigens. Unexpectedly, AHR-deficient HCmel12 melanomas exhibited more frequent delayed resistance to CD8 ACT despite initially impaired tumor growth. To investigate potential underlying mechanisms, we examined the responses of AHR-competent and AHR-deficient melanoma cells to prolonged interferon-{gamma} (IFN{gamma}) exposure. AHR-deficient cells initially exhibited enhanced IFN{gamma}-responsive transcription but progressively lost responsiveness during chronic stimulation, accompanied by reduced MHC class I and II surface expression. Transcriptomic analyses revealed a decline in IFN{gamma}-responsive gene expression and reduced expression of JAK/STAT signaling components, including JAK1. Treatment with the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor decitabine partially restored MHC expression, suggesting a potential contribution of epigenetic regulation. Despite their impaired responsiveness to prolonged IFN{gamma} exposure, AHR-deficient melanoma cells remained susceptible to alternative inflammatory cytotoxic mechanisms. Importantly, CD4 ACT, which can engage broader anti-tumor effector mechanisms, eradicated AHR-deficient melanomas. Together, these findings identify an unexpected role of tumor cell-intrinsic AHR in sustaining IFN{gamma} responsiveness during prolonged inflammatory exposure and reveal distinct outcomes of CD8- and CD4 T-cell-mediated melanoma control.

papers.title: Dual C5aR1 and C5aR2 deficiency uncouples neutrophilic inflammation from antibacterial host defense
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a major cause of bacterial pneumonia and mortality worldwide. While host defense critically depends on complement activation, how C5aR1 and C5aR2 orchestrate pulmonary antibacterial immunity remains unclear. We identified alveolar type II epithelial cells as a local source of C5 and confirmed increased susceptibility of C5-deficient mice to infection. Combined C5aR1/C5aR2 deficiency abolished C5a-induced lung inflammation but paradoxically exacerbated neutrophil accumulation during pneumococcal infection, exceeding that observed in either single-receptor deficiency. Despite their abundance, neutrophils exhibited impaired bacterial clearance, excessive extracellular trap formation, accompanied by aggravated lung injury and mortality. CITE-seq revealed profound neutrophil and macrophage dysregulation, identifying distinct neutrophil subclusters with defective antimicrobial programs, increased cell death and altered inflammatory signatures, consistent with functional exhaustion. Thus, C5aR1 and C5aR2 exert complementary, partially non-redundant functions that couple neutrophil recruitment to antimicrobial competence, prevent excessive inflammation, and preserve effective pulmonary host defense.

papers.title: Antibody-Fcγ receptor-driven NOX2 activation during phagocytosis of tumor cells is suppressed by CD47, preventing CD8 T cell engagement and immunotherapeutic responses.
papers.abstract: Antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) contributes to the elimination of antibody-opsonized tumor cells and engagement of adaptive immunity. This process is inhibited by tumor-cell overexpression of CD47. Here, genome-wide CRISPR screens in macrophages identified the NADPH oxidase (NOX2 complex) and the CD47 receptor, SIRP, as regulators of phagosome acidification. Target-cell CD47 suppressed NOX2 generation of reactive oxygen species at antibody densities that support ADCP, revealing distinct CD47-dependent thresholds for ADCP and oxidant generation. CD47 removal from the target cell delayed phagosome acidification in wild-type macrophages, but not in NOX2-deficient macrophages. Consistent with a role for this pathway in antitumor immunity, tumor-opsonizing anti-Tyrp1 therapy allowed clearance of CD47-deficient B16F10 melanoma tumors in approximately 36% of wild-type mice but failed in NOX2-deficient mice. Tumor clearance required CD8 T cells and IFN{gamma}, but perforin was dispensable. CD4 T cell depletion markedly improved tumor clearance. These findings suggest a noncanonical role for CD8 T cells in supporting ADCP-mediated tumor control. Combining anti-Tyrp1 with a mouse-serum-albumin-IL-2 fusion (MSA-IL-2) or PD-1 blockade enabled superior clearance of CD47-deficient tumors in NOX2-deficient mice, but not wild-type mice. Rechallenge experiments distinguished primary tumor clearance from durable immunity, whereby NOX2-deficient mice treated with anti-Tyrp1 and PD-1 blockade lacked rechallenge protection despite high initial cure rates. Conversely, the addition of MSA-IL-2 supported durable protection in both wild-type and NOX2-deficient mice. These results indicate that tumor CD47 functions beyond a "don't-eat-me" signal by controlling NOX2 activity to positively and negatively regulate CD 8 T cell function. Significance CD47-SIRP suppresses NOX2 activation, regulating a critical feedback loop between ADCP and CD8 T cell activation during tumor-opsonizing antibody therapy, suggesting new strategies for cancer immunotherapy targeting tumor surface antigens.

papers.title: Immunometabolic IRG1-NLRC5 Axis Controls Inflammatory Cell Death
papers.abstract: Innate immunity is the first defense against pathogens, sterile injury, and homeostatic perturbations. One key mechanism used by the innate immune system for host defense is inflammatory cell death, PANoptosis, which eliminates infected or damaged cells and releases cytokines and other danger signals that can further propagate the immune response. Given these inflammatory functions, PANoptosis must be tightly regulated to prevent excess inflammation and pathology. Cellular metabolism is a key regulator of innate immunity, yet how metabolic reprogramming regulates innate immune signaling to control cell death, inflammation, and disease remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the immune-responsive gene 1 (IRG1)-itaconate axis as a critical regulator of PANoptosis. Innate immune triggers robustly induced IRG1 expression, leading to itaconate accumulation and driving IRG1-dependent inflammatory cell death. Mechanistically, glutaminolysis fueled IRG1-dependent itaconate synthesis, and inhibition of glutamine metabolism reduced itaconate accumulation and blocked PANoptosis. Furthermore, NAD depletion, a known inducer of NLRC5-mediated PANoptosis that has been connected to hemolytic, infectious, and inflammatory conditions, acted upstream inducing IRG1 expression and promoting NLRC5-PANoptosome assembly. Together, these findings highlight IRG1 as a metabolic node linking innate immunity to PANoptosis, identifying IRG1 as a potential therapeutic target in hemolytic and inflammatory diseases.

papers.title: Single-cell analysis identifies concurrent type 2 and interferon programs in experimental eosinophilic esophagitis
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, type 2 cytokine-driven allergic disease of the esophagus. How the immune and structural cell landscape of the esophagus changes between healthy and inflamed tissue requires further investigation. Methods: CD45-enriched esophageal cells from naive and oxazolone (OXA)-challenged wild-type mice were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. A cytokine-gated gene expression score identified type 2 program-high cells. Findings were compared with published human esophageal datasets, validated histologically, and examined in Il13ra1-/- mice. Results: A total of 62,245 esophageal cells were analyzed. ILC2s accounted for most type 2 cytokine-expressing lymphocytes in naive mice, whereas Th2 cells accounted for approximately 80% following OXA challenge. ILC2s concurrently lost Il5, Il13 and Gata3 expression while retaining Areg. Resident memory-like CD8 T cells became the largest lymphoid population. Mast cells switched from a connective tissue-type to a mucosal-type and partly cycling state, which was confirmed by increased MCPT1 cells. Esophageal eosinophils displayed a signature resembling skin eosinophils of atopic dermatitis rather than gastrointestinal eosinophils. Il13ra1-/- mice were protected from epithelial proliferation, thickening and eosinophilia. An interferon-associated program characterized lymphoid, myeloid and structural compartments, and its epithelial component was conserved in human EoE. Conclusions: Th2 cells and mucosal-type mast cells are the dominant sources of type 2 cytokines in experimental EoE. This study further identifies a conserved interferon-associated program that accompanies the type 2 response in the immune and structural compartments of the esophagus and highlights it as a candidate contributor to EoE pathology.

papers.title: IPF Patient Derived Lung Macrophages are Crucial In Signaling Fibroblast Activation and Disease Pathogenesis
papers.abstract: The role of lung macrophage-generated paracrine signals such as TGFb in activating fibroblasts in the pathogenesis of Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in humans remains uncertain. Here, employing lung macrophages derived from Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients and genomic, proteomic and cell function analysis of macrophages, we showed increased generation of TGFb over a period of 48 hours indicative of aberrantly activated macrophages. In cell culture studies, we demonstrated that macrophages markedly activated lung fibroblasts. By inducing actin reorganization in fibroblasts coupled to increased membrane tension, cell contractility, and expression of alpha-smooth muscle actin (SMA) and fibroblast activation protein (FAP). Genomic analysis further revealed augmented collagen synthesis, extracellular matrix (ECM) crosslinking, and activation of pro-survival pathways. IPF macrophages exhibited a threefold increase in surface expression of the mannose receptor CD206, which we exploited using mannose-decorated nanoparticles to selectively deliver TGFb siRNA. The nanoparticle mediated TGFb siRNA delivery prevented these manifestations of fibroblast activation. Genomic analysis showed that TGFb promoted FOXO-mediated expression of COL1A1 in fibroblasts coupled to decreased expression of Matrix Metalloproteinases MMP2 and MMP11. Together, these findings establish macrophage-derived TGFb as a key driver of fibroblast activation in human IPF and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of macrophage-targeted nanoparticle-mediated gene silencing.

papers.title: Filtration attenuates cannabis smoke-induced impacts on primary human airway epithelial cells
papers.abstract: Rationale: Combustion of cannabis flower and inhalation into the lungs exposes the airway epithelium to toxic particulates and gases. Whether cigarette-style cellulose-acetate filtration, a standard for tobacco cigarettes, attenuates epithelial injury and how it affects cannabinoid capture remain unclear. Methods: Primary human bronchial epithelial cells from four donors were differentiated at air-liquid interface for 30 days and exposed to three cycles of air or CBD- (12.5%) or THC-dominant (20.2%) cannabis smoke generated with or without a cellulose-acetate filter. Barrier function, epithelial denudation, mediator release and epithelial cell protein markers were assessed. Cannabinoids captured from combustion trials of CBD and THC-dominant cannabis were quantified by LC-MS/MS. Results: Repeated exposure to THC or CBD-dominant cannabis strains decreased barrier function, increased epithelial cell denudation, and resulted in greater cell death. Filtration significantly impeded changes in barrier function, epithelial denudation, and cell-death after exposure to both cannabis products. Filtration reduced THC smoke-induced IL-33, Fas, and TRAIL. Soluble CBD and THC concentrations did not differ significantly between filtered and unfiltered combustion. Despite reducing acute epithelial cell injury and mediator release, filtered smoke did not prevent changes in epithelial cell marker expression profiles. Conclusion: Cellulose-acetate filtration attenuated acute cannabis-smoke-induced epithelial injury and selected mediator responses but did not prevent changes in epithelial cell marker expression profiles associated with differentiated cell states. Measured soluble cannabinoid concentrations did not differ significantly between filtered and unfiltered combustion experiments. Cellulose-acetate filters therefore present a promising harm-reduction strategy for cannabis flower combustion, although it should be noted that like tobacco smoke, negative impacts of cannabis combustion are likely to persist even with filtration.

papers.title: B cell tolerance is dysregulated in people with complex regional pain syndrome: A high-dimensional immunophenotyping study
papers.abstract: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a devastating chronic pain disorder that typically arises after distal limb trauma. It has a complex, multi-system pathophysiology that is not well understood, preventing the development of targeted therapies. Observations of self-reactive antibodies in CRPS patients that can elicit pain hypersensitivity in rodents have established an autoimmune contribution to the onset and maintenance of CRPS-like pain, although the mechanisms underlying this remain unclear. To understand the development of pathogenic autoantibody responses in CRPS, this study performed the first high-dimensional characterisation of B cell activity in a cohort of 42 CRPS patients and 42 matched healthy controls. Immunophenotyping of peripheral immune cell populations by mass cytometry identified altered frequencies of class-switched and double-negative memory B cell subsets in CRPS, and increased use of autoimmune-associated IGHV1-69 and IGHV4-34 gene-encoded heavy-chains within the class-switched B cell compartment. Additional proteomic and autoantibody assessments identified differences in serum protein and IgA autoantibody profiles that may lead to altered complement signalling and pro-inflammatory cytokine production in CRPS. Together, these findings represent evidence of dysregulated B cell self-tolerance in CRPS that could facilitate production of pathogenic autoantibodies in people with the condition.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of T cells across murine lymphoid, mucosal, and gland tissues
papers.abstract: T cells play essential roles in immune surveillance, host defense, and tissue homeostasis, with their cellular composition and transcriptional states varying across tissues. In this study, we constructed an integrated single-cell transcriptional atlas of 124,186 T cells from seven organs of healthy mice. We identified shared T cell states with distinct tissue associated distributions and transcriptional features. Further analyses revealed transcriptional changes associated with thymocyte maturation, diverse innate-like and memory-like T cell populations in bone marrow, and distinct regional distributions of CD8-like T cell states in the intestine. The submandibular gland contained diverse naive, helper-associated, and effector-associated T cell states. pySCENIC analysis further revealed tissue associated variation in inferred transcription factor regulon activity within shared T cell populations. Together, these findings provide a single cell reference for understanding T cell heterogeneity across lymphoid and non-lymphoid tissues under physiological conditions.

papers.title: Keratinocyte IL-17RA signaling promotes neutrophil recruitment and clinical lesions in experimental epidermolysis bullosa
papers.abstract: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) is an autoimmune blistering disease (AIBD) characterized by anti-type VII collagen autoantibody-mediated tissue injury. Neutrophils have been identified as essential for dermal-epidermal separation in various in vitro and mouse models of EBA. Although interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling promotes neutrophilic inflammation, its contribution to EBA and the relevant responding cell types remain poorly defined. We investigated the role and cellular targets of IL-17 receptor A (IL-17RA) signaling using an antibody-transfer model of EBA in mice with global IL-17RA deficiency, combined IL-17A/IL-17F deficiency, IL-17F deficiency, or myeloid cell- or keratinocyte-specific IL-17RA deletion. Complementary in vitro assays assessed IL-17A-induced chemokine expression and neutrophil migration. Global IL-17RA deficiency, combined IL-17A/IL-17F deficiency, and IL-17F deficiency significantly reduced disease severity in vivo. Keratinocyte-specific IL-17RA deletion markedly attenuated EBA, whereas myeloid cell-specific deletion did not confer protection. In vitro, IL-17A increased Cxcl1 mRNA expression in keratinocytes and fibroblasts, and conditioned media from stimulated cells promoted neutrophil migration. These findings identify keratinocytes as key cellular targets of IL-17RA signaling in experimental EBA and support a mechanism linking epithelial cytokine responses to neutrophil recruitment and tissue injury. Our data support investigating the keratinocyte IL-17RA pathway as a potential therapeutic target in EBA and related AIBD.

papers.title: GRABS: a content-addressed antibody-antigen binding-affinity dataset with predicted structures and a leak-free benchmark
papers.abstract: Machine-learning prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity depends as much on the training data as on the model, yet public affinity measurements are scattered across databases with incompatible formats, mix genuine dissociation constants with censored or predicted values, and concentrate most of their label mass on a few heavily mutated targets. We present GRABS (Geometric Resource for Antibody Binding Studies), a curated, content-addressed, structure-ready dataset that consolidates nine public sources, of which the seven with redistributable licenses yield 4,380 canonical antibody-antigen records} (median-collapsed from 4,761 raw measurements), each with an experimentally measured dissociation constant (Kd), paired heavy and light variable regions (VH, VL), and an antigen sequence, covering 2,015 distinct antigen sequences. Every structure, graph, and feature is addressed by a content key, md5(VH+VL+antigen)[:10], and verified non-circularly: each graph's node features are decoded back to sequence and re-hashed, matching the content key for 4,282/4,282 (100%) structure-backed records. This integrity is load-bearing: an alignment ablation shows that a previously-reported strong cross-target result (R2 {approx} 0.415) was a misalignment-mediated source/batch leak that content-key regeneration dissolves. On the resulting leak-free, antigen-cluster-grouped benchmark, cross-target ranking of variants of a held-out antigen collapses to the noise floor (within-held-out-antigen Spearman {rho} {approx} 0 for every model family: sequence, structure, and folding-confidence), with structure giving no advantage, a rigorously leakage-controlled quantification of the limited reach of current methods. GRABS ships model-ready artifacts (Boltz-2 predicted complexes, per-residue ESM-2 embeddings, geometric graphs, feature vectors) with antigen-stratified splits, and is intended for leakage-free benchmarking and within-target affinity ranking (measure-then-rank), not zero-shot prediction for antigens absent from training.

papers.title: Drastic improvement in MHC class I epitope prediction through training data augmentation, generative adversarial network modeling of selfness, and consideration of homology to class II epitopes.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of immunogenic neoantigens is critical for personalized cancer vaccines but remains hindered by the high false-positive rates of current predictors. Here, we present DeepOmicsNeo, a modular deep learning framework that harmonizes three biological determinants of immunogenicity. The first module, DeepOmicsNeo-Binding, overcomes data scarcity in non-9mer peptide-Class I Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) binding prediction via a novel augmentation strategy that synthesizes pseudo-binders and non-binders by editing non-anchor residues, outperforming its competitors. The second module, DeepOmicsNeo-Selfness, addresses the paucity of negative training data for immunogenicity prediction by utilizing a Generative Adversarial Network trained on around 60 million human self-peptides. This unsupervised approach quantifies selfness to detect immunogenic peptides and the resulting score correlated with IFN-{gamma} secretion by T-cells. The third module, DeepOmicsNeo-H2, exploits the central-region homology between known HLA Class-I and Class-II restricted epitopes. The integrated model, DeepOmicsNeo-Immunogenicity, outperforms state-of-the-art predictors on the TESLA, HiTIDE, and TiTANIAN benchmark datasets.[2.1] Top20 precision, the most important benchmark for clinical utility in personalized cancer vaccine design, was drastically improved over other predictors. Together, these findings indicate that jointly modeling the three complementary features captures biologically meaningful determinants of immunogenicity, supporting DeepOmicsNeo as a robust computational framework for neoantigen prioritization in personalized cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Overcoming subtype-specific immune resistance in small cell lung cancer through RNA-based immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) comprises neuroendocrine (NE) and non-neuroendocrine (non-NE) subtypes with distinct immune landscapes and responses to therapy. Here, we established murine experimental metastases models to investigate RNA vaccination across SCLC subtypes. These exhibited distinct organotrophic properties and differ in both the magnitude and kinetics of interferon-induced MHC-I upregulation. Vaccination controlled non-NE tumors but provided limited survival benefit against NE tumors established in the lung or liver. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and chromatin accessibility profiling revealed inflammation-associated programs following vaccination shared between organs. To overcome the limited survival benefit of vaccination in NE SCLC, we combined RNA vaccination with liver-targeted RNA-encoded cytokines. This combination markedly prolonged survival of NE tumor-bearing mice and enhanced inflammatory immune activity within the tumor microenvironment. Together, these findings identify vaccination-associated inflammatory programs of potential clinical relevance and warrant further investigation of cytokine combination therapy as strategy to improve immunotherapy in NE SCLC.

papers.title: Measuring the information budget of cross-target antibody affinity generalization: a robust cross-target wall, and why structure reaches developability but not affinity
papers.abstract: Structure-based machine learning is widely expected to advance antibody engineering, yet it is unclear how far affinity predictions transfer to new targets, and why. We introduce a noise-corrected, censoring-aware estimator of the cross-target transfer ceiling, {rho}max = {surd}(T/(T+I)), which separates a transferable antibody-intrinsic component (T) from a non-transferable target-specific interaction (I). On deterministic synthetic ground truth the estimator recovers the noise-free ceiling to {+/-} 0.0003, whereas the naive sum-of-squares estimator is biased downward by measurement noise. Applying it from synthetic to real systems, the transferable budget is small, and on real neutralization panels it is not an artefact: the target-specific interaction survives noise and censoring correction. It is strongly regime-dependent, with a two-tier structure: predicting a novel antibody from sequence alone (the design setting) reaches a lower ceiling ({rho} {approx} 0.44 on real breadth data) than ranking a characterized one ({rho} {approx} 0.59), even with a strong protein language model. Synthetic oracles also overstate transferability: an oracle scored on real predicted structures carries about half the budget of a matched synthetic lattice (0.45 vs. 0.81), and real neutralization and escape panels sit well below the synthetic ceiling (0.32-0.68). Under leakage-free antigen-cluster splits, cross-target affinity ranking across every method family collapses to this budget, while within a sampled target a structure-based graph network ranks affinity above off-the-shelf FoldX and GearBind (within-complex Spearman 0.55), and structural surface descriptors predict a surface-driven developability property (hydrophobic aggregation) where sequence-dominated properties (humanness, charge-driven self-association) do not benefit. A controlled ablation attributes the residual within-target signal to the antibody alone: dropping the antigen from the structural model leaves it essentially unchanged (interface {Delta} {rho} between -0.01 and +0.02 across four panels), so for this model the paratope-epitope interface adds no ranking signal over the antibody alone. Models climb toward the budget within a target -- via a measure-then-rank operating mode that recovers top binders 6-8 times more efficiently than random once a target has been sampled -- but none crosses it.

papers.title: Switch from inflammatory signaling to excessive extracellular matrix remodeling in fibrotic fibroblasts attenuates monocyte tissue infiltration
papers.abstract: Tissue damage induces infiltration of monocytes that differentiate into macrophages and cooperate with fibroblasts in tissue repair. If repair fails and tissue stress persists, a feedforward loop involving high contractility of activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, and TGF-{beta}1 signaling can lead to chronic fibrosis characterized by hypertrophic scarring. In advanced fibrotic tissues areas devoid of immune infiltration have been detected but how the interplay between chemotactic signals versus ECM remodeling impacts monocyte infiltration and spatial positioning in such late-stage fibrotic tissues is unresolved. To address this, we designed a series of 3D co-culture formats incorporating fibrillar collagen I-based ECM, human fibroblasts, and primary human monocytes. RNA-seq, secretome analysis, and confocal microscopy showed that collagen-embedded fibroblasts strongly upregulated inflammatory signaling compared to 2D fibroblast cultures. Incorporation of fibroblasts enhanced collagen fiber network porosity and stimulated monocyte entry into collagen hydrogels and their migration within the collagen network. TGF-{beta}1 activation of collagen-embedded fibroblasts caused a striking switch from inflammatory signaling to an ECM remodeling signature, which was accompanied by local ECM accumulation around fibroblasts and a pronounced increase in collagen fiber network pore size. This did not affect overall fibroblast-stimulated monocyte migration through the ECM, but it prevented monocytes from crossing liquid-hydrogel barriers to penetrate the collagen network. Moreover, it caused excessive ECM remodeling near clusters of fibroblasts, which locally arrested monocyte migration. These findings indicate that excessive fibroblast activation in fibrotic tissues can shift the balance from chemotactic cues toward biomechanical constraints, which limits monocyte infiltration and locally restricts monocyte migration.

papers.title: Cell identity and activation state determine the innate immune response to nanoplastics
papers.abstract: Autoimmune disease is on the rise, and while no direct connection has been made, evidence suggests environmental toxins such as nanoplastics may be contributing to the increased incidence. A key factor in the onset of autoimmunity is inflammation; yet how nanoplastics impact innate immune function is unclear. Here, we exposed primary human neutrophils, macrophages, and endothelial cells to biocorona-coated polystyrene nanoplastics at physiologically relevant concentrations. All cells internalized nanoplastics without viability loss, but functional consequences diverged. Neutrophils increased myeloperoxidase release as nanoplastic concentration increased. Endothelial cells reduced leukocyte-recruiting mediator secretion and had decreased neutrophil adhesion following inflammatory stimulation. M1 macrophages broadly upregulated inflammatory cytokine secretion (including TNF- and IL-6), whereas M0 and M2 macrophages exhibited no significant secretory changes. Collectively, these findings indicate physiologically relevant nanoplastic concentrations do not universally increase inflammation but rather dysregulate innate immune populations in a manner that could contribute to autoimmunity.

papers.title: Continuous generation of short-lived resident effector CD8 T cells sustains alopecia areata
papers.abstract: CD8 T cells mediating chronic tissue inflammation have been thought to depend on stem-like progenitors that self-renew and replenish cytotoxic effector cells or exhausted progeny. Here, we show that stem-independent, short-lived resident effector CD8 T (TRE) cells sustain alopecia areata (AA), a common autoimmune disease that destroys hair follicles. AA-TRE cells exhibit TCR-dependent cytotoxicity, undergo rapid apoptosis in the skin, and lack memory or stem-like properties. Following adoptive transfer, donor TRE cells serve only as an initial trigger, whereas the host-derived CD103CD101 pathogenic pool is rebuilt continuously in skin-draining lymph nodes (sdLNs). Single-cell multiome and CUT&Tag profiling revealed that AA-TRE cells epigenetically silence Tox and upregulate RUNX2 to initiate the TRE differentiation program in sdLNs, while RUNX3 and AP-1s sustain it in the skin. Notably, CD8 T cells from patients with AA share this conserved regulatory network. Altogether, these findings define a distinct CD8 T cell differentiation state, offering new therapeutic implications for autoimmune diseases.
